x: Jack Shields, in the R.A.F. in Buckinghamshire, says " There is very little opportunity for running here." Bill Snell.—On his way overseas, and who has taken his Belgrave togs with him.
Jack Shields is another who turned up at Belgrave Hall, when on Xmas leave and went out for a run. I hope he was not too stiff the next day.

Will all "top-liners" and sports promoters kindly note and keep the date open. Jack Shields has recently returned from Africa, and when on leave called at the Hall for a run with George Still.
Jack Shields and Johnny Briggs went up to Oxford University for the Michaelmas Term and we wish them well academically and athletically.

Good wishes to Basil Walden, on B.O.A.C. duties in Tripoli; John Briggs and Jack Shields, now studying at Oxford University; to Reg. Eddie Short lost a shoe but pluckily kept going and Archie Bedford came through to finish a good fourth. Jack Shields and Ken England were also well up and a new member in J.

Jack Shields, who has been suffering from polio for many weeks, and has lived during that time in an iron lung, is now improving. Many Belgravians have already visited him at Grove Hospital, Tooting, and he will be pleased to see any of his Club mates to help him along his uphill fight towards full recovery.
